The analysis was designed to build situational awareness by bringing together information on feedstock availability, supporting infrastructure, co-location opportunities, and potential market competition to inform decision-making and identify areas where more detailed, site-specific analysis may be warranted. Feedstock availability was quantified within 50- and 100-mile radius of each airport to illustrate the scale of regionally accessible biomass resources. Co-location opportunities were evaluated by identifying nearby landfills, combustion facilities, and closed or idle wood-using mills within approximately 50 miles of each airport, reflecting facilities that may offer existing infrastructure, industrial zoning, or utility access that could reduce development complexity. Supporting transportation infrastructure was assessed based on proximity (within 50 miles) to marine docks and rail loading or transload facilities, which can play a critical role in feedstock and product logistics. To provide market context, the analysis also identified active wood-using mills and existing bioenergy facilities within 50 miles of each airport. These facilities may rely on similar feedstock resources and therefore represent potential competition that could influence feedstock availability, pricing, or procurement strategies. Table 7 summarizes these indicators for each airport location, presenting total biomass resources within defined collection radius alongside the presence of relevant infrastructure, co-location assets, and competing facilities. Collectively, this integrated view is intended to support informed planning discussions, highlight opportunities and constraints unique to each location, and guide subsequent, more detailed feasibility and techno-economic assessments.
